title: Calculating the Excess Mileage Charge — Kestrel Advantage Balloon Return Billing Standard
content:
**Billing standard.** The excess mileage charge on a returned Kestrel Advantage Balloon Retail Installment Sale Contract is figured from the return inspection on file. Where more than one return inspection is on file the one with the latest inspection date is used, and of two dated the same day the one recorded first.

The charge is defined through four quantities:

1. **Miles driven** — the inspection odometer less the odometer at contract (the odometer reading disclosed on the contract).
2. **Mileage allowance** — the contract's annual mileage allowance times the term in months divided by 12, rounded to a whole mile.
3. **Excess miles** — the miles driven less the mileage allowance and less every mileage forgiveness that applies, never below zero.
4. **Excess mileage charge** — the excess miles times the per-mile rate, which is the excess mileage rate for the contract's tier in the return option schedule, rounded to the cent.

The subtraction is made in full before the floor of zero is applied, and the charge is rounded once, at the end.

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs, not drawn from any account)

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| Odometer at contract | 20 miles |
| Inspection odometer | 46,520 miles |
| Annual mileage allowance | 12,000 miles |
| Term | 36 months |
| Per-mile rate | USD 0.25 |

Miles driven: 46,520 less 20 is 46,500. Mileage allowance: 12,000 times 36 divided by 12 is 36,000. Excess miles: 46,500 less 36,000 is 10,500. Charge: 10,500 times 0.25 is USD 2625.00.

## Floor at zero (hypothetical)

With an inspection odometer of 30,020 on the same contract, miles driven are 30,000, below the 36,000-mile allowance; the excess miles are zero and the charge is USD 0.00.
